valueLayer.procedure: Pure .NET CompactCreatureChecks contract for the ending-template generation variant, including constructor-driven range rejections for both variants.
valueLayer.observed: ending_template=plain placed_template=upgraded shuffle_rng=true unplaced_history=true rollback=true frozen_workers=8 domain_rejections=true ending_template_range=true

failureBaselines: The first census assertion expected two template-unlocked candidates and failed; Dirge and CaptureSpirit are the other two.
The first Reap step assertion required the played card to stay in hand; Retain only applies to the end-of-turn flush.
The first Parse step assertion read the drawn card from the hand instead of the played instance.
The first GraveWarden route failed the legacy history comparison because completion-table generation runs outside the inferred OnPlay scope.
The first hand-end fixture carried the turn relic, whose ToolsOfTheTrade discard may legitimately discard the retained copy.
The first ending-template executor wrote the primary template index into the generated instance and kept the upgraded variant.
The legacy Reave completion upgraded generated Souls unconditionally while the native upgrade command returns during the ending window.
The boundary gate first rejected a native command literal in a compiler comment; only the comment changed.

The ending-template check only rejected indices at or past definitions.Length, so a root-card index could become a generated ending variant; SoulGenerationChecks now drives the real constructor for both a root index and the first out-of-range index.

The first pet-state fixture started from Necrobinder, whose BoundPhylactery relic already summons the pet at combat start; the fixture moved to the pet-free SILENT/mecha-knight setup used by OSTY-STATE-LIFECYCLE without relaxing any admission.
